name: Genubath
overview: Genubath is a male figure known primarily as the son of Hadad, mentioned in 1 Kings 11:20. There is no additional information about his tribe or other distinguishing notes in Scripture. His mention is brief and focused on his lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Genubath means "thief" and is a proper name recorded in 1 Kings 11:20. This meaning is given in the biblical text but was not assigned by God. No further titles are associated with him.
familyAndRelationships: Genubath is explicitly identified as the son of Hadad according to 1 Kings 11:20. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not record any other family connections for Genubath.
scriptureSignificance: Genubath's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his identity as the son of Hadad, a figure mentioned in the context of King Solomon's reign. His mention serves to highlight the continuation of Hadad's line, though Genubath himself is not elaborated upon in Scripture. This brief reference underscores the historical and genealogical details important to the biblical record.
